prompts.prompt: Edit this FRONT COVER ART reference, keeping its overall composition, near-black background and muted antique gold/sepia appearance. Transform the rendering decisively into true copperplate etching: Piranesi-like fine crossed hatching, deep architectural shadows made of lines, dramatic spatial recession; Georg Pencz-like crisp contour and humane legible gestures. This is an original homage, no copied historical print. The SUBJECT MUST REMAIN BRAZILIAN, rooted in the novel Molambudos: a battered closed leather diary with a completely blank label, blank archival papers and a small sepia fictional photograph of a rural Brazilian boy, never a real recognizable person; cracked dry sertão soil, cacti (mandacaru and xique-xique), thorny leafless caatinga; a Rasga Mortalha barn owl with clear heart-shaped pale face; in the distance a modest early-20th-century Brazilian institutional hospital building with stucco facade and clay roof tiles, its corridor transformed into oppressive depth through arches and iron-barred windows. NO European castle, no Gothic cathedral, no medieval dungeon, no Roman aqueduct, no Renaissance costume. Keep diary at lower center and owl at mid-right, let dry branches frame the left. A tiny discreet carmine ribbon on the diary is the sole chromatic accent beyond black/sepia/gold. Top 33 percent remains empty nearly black for title added separately; bottom 17 percent remains empty nearly black for author credits. Middle art should clearly look DRAWN WITH ENGRAVED LINES, not photograph, not painterly digital rendering, not embossed leather photorealism. Preserve portrait 2:3 canvas, 1024x1536 or higher native size, precise lines for print. Absolutely NO TEXT, NO letters or numbers, no signatures, no institution signage, no logo, no barcode, no border. No gore, no injured child, no real historical evidence. Fictional literary horror with dignity.

Edit this BACK COVER ART reference to make the linework unmistakably an original copperplate etching combining Piranesi's hatching, institutional spatial oppression and chiaroscuro with Georg Pencz's precise contours. Keep the existing dark almost-black, muted antique gold/sepia palette and the quiet large negative-space composition. Make the setting Brazilian: a decaying early-20th-century Brazilian asylum corridor of limewashed stucco, modest rounded plaster arches, clay-tile roofing hinted through an opening, iron-barred windows, no Gothic cathedral, no European castle, no Roman monumental ruin. At lower left, one delicate feather of the Rasga Mortalha barn owl over blank archival papers, cracked sertão earth and dry caatinga twigs with a small mandacaru silhouette. No human portrait is necessary. A single tiny muted carmine thread tied to the feather is the only chromatic accent. Upper and central 70 percent must remain near-black, uniformly low contrast and open for typeset synopsis; bottom-right quarter empty near-black for barcode reserve added later. Art concentrated at lower left and a faint corridor along outer edges. Fine crisp etched cross-hatching and no smooth painterly digital airbrush; subdued but printable line detail. Preserve portrait 2:3 canvas, 1024x1536 or higher native resolution. Absolutely no text, no pseudo-writing, no numbers, no signatures, no logos, no frame, no barcode. Entirely fictional Brazilian literary horror, no real historical document, no identifiable real victim, no gore.
